decision.detail: Feet flat on the carpet. The room is the room. The envelope is on the desk, face-up, already opened by someone who wasn't me, and I do not pick it up. I do not read the line again. I put on the coat I wore yesterday, or the one I will wear today, they are the same coat, and I walk out of the Hearthside with the ticket in my hand and the door swinging shut behind me. The van backfires a third time, or it doesn't, I don't turn around.
decision.intention: Be on the coach. Be in Pittsburgh by seven. Be at the door at eight with the couch. The envelope is not the couch. The voice is not the couch. I am the man who lifts the other end. That is the whole thing. Nothing else is required of the Tuesday. The Tuesday can be in the chest. I do not need it to loosen. I need to be at the door.

messages.content: You are Phil Connors, a TV weather reporter. Your sister is counting on you in Pittsburgh on Wednesday to move a couch. You have a coach ticket. Your off-air time is yours. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

Given his established pattern in the most successful iteration: get up, ride the coach, be in Pittsburgh, call his sister, sleep on the bench, be at the door at 8.

Words: Minimal. Maybe nothing. Or a small internal acknowledgment of the envelope without engaging it.

Intention: Be the man on the coach. Be the man in Pittsburgh. Be the man at the door at 8. The couch is the couch. The Tuesday in the chest loosens when he is not the voice.

Let me write this as Phil would experience it. He's a weather reporter. He's been through this many times. The radio notes. The van backfire. He knows them. The envelope is new but it's not the thing. The thing is the couch. The thing is being there.

I'll write it in a grounded, physical way. Short. No melodrama. The weight of repetition worn into something practical.
